playtest.entry: Playtest: actual Main offline city running in GLFW under Xvfb Mesa, with real xdotool input and production F10 recorder.
playtest.browser: Voxel One is a native game; browser playtesting does not apply.
playtest.setup: Synthetic live ECS fixture. Automatic household replanning held with retryAt infinity; production CitySimulation.travel invoked for 0.1-second steps while the real engine renders the world, travellers, horses and HUD. This isolates traffic behavior from job scheduling.
steps: Launch fresh synthetic offline city, focus real X11 game window, close controls menu when present. Focus city camera and zoom to 256.

Place three pedestrians .65 metres apart on forward pavement z=25.75; place reverse pedestrian on z=23.25. Hold leader. Advance followers once: positions remain unchanged and activity becomes Waiting for traffic.

Advance reverse traveller while leader is held; it moves freely. Release leader, run 20 steps with 250 ms visual spacing between steps; verify every queued traveller advances, no overtaking, minimum .5 metre gap, retained routes and correct lanes.
Repeat with mounted citizens on carriageway lanes z=25 and z=24, initial 1 metre spacing and minimum .65 metre gap.

Place two pedestrians on perpendicular approaches near (8.5,24.5). Run 30 steps in each update order with 150 ms visual spacing. Verify yielding traveller backs out to free priority stopping space, gap stays at least .5 metres, no Route obstructed state, and both routes finish.

Use real F10 key events to start and stop each recording. Save actual window screenshots before and after each scenario. Decode each clip at its first, middle and last frames and inspect those frames.
playtest.expected: Congested forward travellers wait behind the held leader and resume in order; reverse lane remains free; crossing yields without deadlock or collision.
playtest.observed: All runtime assertions passed. Fresh close-view screenshots and decoded F10 frames visually show waiting queues, queue release, separate travel directions and completed crossings.
playtest.limits: Synthetic fixture control is explicit. Software rendering ran near 2–4 FPS; this is behavior evidence, not a performance benchmark.
